# Proverbs 28 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** [The]-wicked flee and-no-one pursues, but-[the]-righteous [are]-bold like-a-young-lion.

**2** By-[the]-transgression-of a-land many [are] its-princes, but-by-a-man-of understanding [and]-knowledge, so [the]-established-order endures.

**3** A-man poor and-oppressing poor-ones — a-rain washing-away and-no bread.

**4** Those-forsaking [the]-law praise [the]-wicked, but-those-keeping [the]-law contend with-them.

**5** Men-of evil do-not-understand justice, but-those-seeking YHWH understand everything.

**6** Better [is] a-poor-man walking in-his-integrity, than-one-twisted-of ways — and-he [is] rich.

**7** One-keeping [the]-law [is] a-son [who]-understands, but-a-companion-of gluttons shames his-father.

**8** One-increasing his-wealth by-interest and-usury — for-one-showing-grace to-[the]-poor he-gathers-it.

**9** One-turning-away his-ear from-hearing [the]-law — even his-prayer [is an]-abomination.

**10** One-leading [the]-upright astray in-a-way evil — into-his-[own]-pit he will-fall, but-[the]-blameless will-inherit good.

**11** Wise in-his-[own]-eyes [is the]-man rich, but-a-poor-man [who]-has-understanding searches-him-out.

**12** When-[the]-righteous triumph great [is the]-glory, but-when-[the]-wicked rise people hide-themselves.

**13** One-concealing his-transgressions will-not-prosper, but-one-confessing and-forsaking will-find-compassion.

**14** Blessed [is the]-man [who]-fears always, but-one-hardening his-heart will-fall into-evil.

**15** A-lion roaring and-a-bear charging — a-ruler wicked over a-people poor.

**16** A-ruler lacking-of understanding — also great-of oppressions; one-hating unjust-gain will-lengthen days.

**17** A-man burdened [with the]-blood-of a-soul — to the-pit let-him-flee; let-them-not-support-him.

**18** One-walking [in]-integrity will-be-saved, but-one-twisted-of ways will-fall in-one [of them].

**19** One-working his-ground will-be-satisfied [with]-bread, but-one-pursuing empty-things will-be-satisfied [with]-poverty.

**20** A-man-of faithfulness [has]-many blessings, but-one-hastening to-become-rich will-not-go-unpunished.

**21** To-show-partiality [is]-not good, for-on-account-of a-morsel-of bread a-man will-transgress.

**22** Hastening to-wealth [is] a-man-of evil eye, and-he-does-not-know that lack will-come-to-him.

**23** One-rebuking a-man — afterward he-will-find more favor than-one-flattering [with the]-tongue.

**24** One-robbing his-father and-his-mother and-saying, 'There-is-no transgression' — a-companion he [is] to-a-man-of destruction.

**25** Broad-of soul stirs-up strife, but-one-trusting upon YHWH will-be-made-fat.

**26** One-trusting in-his-[own]-heart — he [is] a-fool, but-one-walking in-wisdom — he will-be-delivered.

**27** One-giving to-[the]-poor — there-is-no lack, but-one-hiding his-eyes — many curses.

**28** When-[the]-wicked rise people hide-themselves, but-when-they-perish [the]-righteous increase.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **28:1**: Yanus rasha ve-ein rodef — 'flees the wicked and no one pursues.' Guilt creates its own prison; righteousness produces boldness.

- **28:13**: Mekhasseh fesha'av lo yatzliach — 'one concealing his transgressions will not prosper.' The most direct confession-and-repentance proverb in the collection.

- **28:26**: Bote'ach be-libbo hu kesil — 'trusting in his own heart, he is a fool.' Directly challenges the modern ethic of 'follow your heart.'

— EMET
